page: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Dldsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, the processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average to strong performance across various compute and memory workloads. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2163.0 and a multi-core score of 13256.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 26706.63. Single-threaded gzip compression performs strongly at 31.37 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 104.48 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1240.45 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 125.11 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For machine learning tasks, the hardware demonstrates top-tier performance in text generation using a small 135M LLM model, reaching 396.44 tokens/sec, though medium 7B model generation is more moderate at 15.67 tokens/sec. The primary tradeoff of this configuration is its low memory density, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D16lds_v6 offers a high-density compute profile with a bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD, reducing the need for external storage attachments for temporary data. This resource balance makes it highly suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. Recommended use cases include software compilation, web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations. It is also well-suited for localized batch processing and small-scale machine learning inference tasks where the Intel AMX instructions can be leveraged.
